title: MIT 6.046: Design and Analysis of Algorithms

unit.title: Algorithm-to-Component Kickoff: Weighted Interval Scheduling

origin.rationale: The catalog describes an emphasis on algorithm design and analysis and names Python, but it does not provide verified lesson-level content. This bridging unit combines proof, implementation, contracts, and deterministic testing without claiming to reproduce an MIT unit.

unit.audience: A strong algorithms student with introductory data structures and algorithms experience who is beginning to build production-oriented software-engineering habits.
prerequisites: Asymptotic notation and basic proof techniques
learning_objectives: Translate an optimization problem into an explicit, testable software contract.
Design and justify a correct weighted interval scheduling algorithm.
Implement deterministic behavior, validation, and non-mutation guarantees in Python.
Use a small exhaustive oracle and fixed-seed generated cases as differential test evidence.
Report correctness, complexity, assumptions, and engineering trade-offs in a concise design note.

requires: All four learner deliverables are present and readable.
The prescribed deterministic test command completes successfully within the validator timeout.
Independent examiner checks confirm contract conformance, optimality, deterministic tie handling, and input validation.
The design note contains a coherent correctness argument and honest end-to-end complexity analysis.
Comprehension responses meet the independent examiner threshold.

course_completion.policy: Passing this unit records only a validator-confirmed unit result. It does not establish coverage of MIT 6.046, the catalog's estimated hours, linked assignments, recordings, or textbook.

decisions: Preserve the discovered course identity and prerequisite level.
Use Python because it is named in the catalog metadata.
Create one self-contained engineering bridge rather than infer an official first lecture or assignment.
Keep all linked or merely described resources optional and unavailable until a later authorized retrieval job verifies them.
